summary: We developed NISAR Mission Control, an interactive web application with an aerospace control-center interface that transforms complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into accessible visual insights. The project addresses the limitations of traditional optical sensors which are obstructed by dense clouds, volcanic ash, or darkness by leveraging microwave radar technology capable of capturing Earth observation data day or night under any weather condition. Focusing on Popocatépetl Volcano and other volcanoes as a case study, the platform enables users to visualize real satellite acquisition footprints from ASF Vertex, compare HH/HV polarizations alongside thermal and soil moisture sensors in real time, and track live natural disaster alerts via EONET. This open solution translates advanced geospatial science into a practical tool for researchers, decision-makers, and public outreach.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? NISAR Mission Control is an interactive web application styled as an aerospace control center that transforms complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into accessible visual insights. Focusing on Popocatépetl Volcano and other volcanoes as a case study, the platform enables users to map real satellite acquisition footprints from repositories like ASF Vertex, switch in real time between polarizations (HH/HV) and complementary sensors (infrared/thermal and soil moisture) to analyze surface roughness and physical behavior, and track live natural events via EONET.

Benefits and intended impact Unlike traditional optical sensors which are obstructed by dense clouds, volcanic ash, or darkness microwave SAR technology captures Earth observation data day and night under any weather condition. This open platform bridges the gap between raw aerospace data and practical usability for three key audiences:

  • Researchers: Fast visual inspection of SAR granules and temporal terrain changes.
  • Decision-makers & civil protection: Continuous volcanic monitoring and natural hazard risk management.
  • General public: Engaging scientific outreach to better understand Earth's dynamic surface.

Tools, programming languages, and software used

  • Frontend & Web Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and interactive geospatial mapping libraries to render coordinates and satellite footprints.
  • Data Sources & APIs: SAR datasets and metadata (NISAR mission / ASF Vertex repository), complementary sensor layers, and live natural event streams (EONET API).
  • UI/UX Design: Custom dark-mode interface inspired by real telemetry and mission-control consoles.

Creativity and key factors considered Our project's creativity lies in blending rigorous radar remote sensing with the intuitive, immersive experience of a live mission-control dashboard, removing the steep learning curve of specialized GIS software. Our team prioritized visual accessibility (high-contrast telemetry styling), zero-installation browser performance, and real-world regional impact by selecting Popocatépetl Volcano as a vital case study for hazard monitoring in Mexico.
